display.title: Mitzvah Time: Why We Cover Our Eyes for the Shema
display.summary_short: Unlike any other prayer, we close our eyes and cover them with the right hand for the Shema, so nothing distracts us from its meaning.
display.summary_long: A short Mitzvah Time lesson from the Tzivos Hashem radio show. Uncle Yossi reveals something we do only for the Shema, not for any other mitzvah or prayer, not even Shemoneh Esrei: we close our eyes and cover them with our right hand. The reason is concentration. If we say the words without thinking of their meaning, especially of the word Echad, we must say the Shema again, so we cover our eyes tightly so that nothing distracts us. We say the Shema slowly, word by word, remembering that the aleph of Echad stands for Hashem, the ches for the seven heavens and the earth, and the dalet for the four directions: Hashem is everywhere and rules everywhere.
display.lesson: Cover your eyes and say the Shema slowly, thinking about every word, especially 'Echad'.
